Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}\cdot 5\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x){|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\cdot 0)] \\  & +\frac{1}{5}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{5})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot 0)] \\  & =(0-0)+\frac{1}{5}(-1-1) \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
